reviewer.notes: Independently re-ran both named probes from a clean checkout of origin/cursor/p2-loop-to-green-0db0 (base_sha 787db20e85ffa9d6e6ab05b5029c84e7eea77d80). FIRST FALSIFICATION ATTEMPT SUCCEEDED THEN WAS RESOLVED: this sandbox does not ship tiktoken by default; running probe1 cold produced tokenizer=fallback-whitespace with full_file_tokens_model=24044 -- a 56% deviation from the artifact's claimed 54643 -- because the probe's get_encoder() silently swallows the ImportError and falls back to a whitespace counter without failing loudly or changing its exit code, so a tiktoken-less environment would silently pack a materially different headline number under the same tokenizer label mismatch would at least be visible (tokenizer field does correctly change to 'fallback-whitespace', so the artifact is not mislabeling, but nothing forces a hard failure if that field goes unchecked). This is a real fragility in the probe (recorded as a new observation below) but does NOT falsify the existing committed artifact: after `pip install tiktoken` the probe reproduced the committed probe1-tokenize-sum.json, probe1-tokenize.raw.txt, probe2-occupancy-compare.json, control-tolerance.json, and probe2-occupancy.raw.txt byte-for-byte (git diff --stat showed zero changes), proving tiktoken WAS the tokenizer actually used to produce the committed receipt evidence, exactly as claimed. SECOND, STRONGER FALSIFICATION ATTEMPT: re-tokenized all 5 full-file injectees with a completely independent library and vocabulary (transformers.GPT2TokenizerFast, not tiktoken) to check whether the cl100k_base numbers are plausible rather than an artifact of one code path. Per-file bytes matched exactly (CLAUDE.md=6714, AGENTS.md=7812, llm-security/AGENTS.md=102687, humanizer/AGENTS.md=1639, code-security/AGENTS.md=112277; total=231129, matching both probes and independent `wc -c`). cl100k_base recompute (own script, own tiktoken.get_encoding call) reproduced 54643 total / 27525 dominant exactly. GPT2-BPE recompute gave 85745 total / 40420 dominant -- higher in absolute terms (GPT-2's older, smaller-vocab BPE is well known to under-merge English prose relative to cl100k_base, so a ~1.57x ratio is the expected direction and rough magnitude, not a red flag) but preserves the SAME dominant-file ranking (code-security/AGENTS.md > llm-security/AGENTS.md > AGENTS.md > CLAUDE.md > humanizer/AGENTS.md) under every one of the four independent measures tried (bytes, cl100k tokens, GPT2-BPE tokens, whitespace words). THIRD FALSIFICATION ATTEMPT: manually recomputed char4_tokens (len(text)//4 per file, bypassing the probe's helper) and occupancy (sum(bytes)//4, bypassing session_occupancy_proxy()) by hand in a fresh script: sum of per-file char4 = 57748 (matches full_file_tokens_char4 exactly) and floor(231129/4) = 57782 (matches occupancy_tokens_char4 exactly); gap = |57748-57782|/57782 = 0.000588, matching the claimed 0.0006 to displayed precision. Confirmed the small non-zero gap is legitimately explained by multi-byte UTF-8 characters (chars < bytes for all 5 files, e.g. code-security/AGENTS.md has 112277 bytes but only 112221 decoded chars) rather than measurement error. FOURTH FALSIFICATION ATTEMPT (both-states control): manually recomputed the bad-state gap by omitting the dominant file's char4 count (28055) from the full char4 sum (57748-28055=29693), giving gap=|29693-57782|/57782=0.4861 > tolerance 0.35 -- control correctly fires on the incomplete-set fixture and stays silent on the complete set, exactly as recorded. FIFTH, SESSION-SPECIFIC FALSIFICATION ATTEMPT: as the actual fresh-context reviewer for this task, I inspected my OWN system prompt's <always_applied_workspace_rules> block (the real turn-0 injection for this session, captured before I opened the audit artifact or the probe source) and it contains exactly five full-file entries -- /workspace/CLAUDE.md, /workspace/AGENTS.md, /workspace/.agents/skills/llm-security/AGENTS.md, /workspace/.agents/skills/humanizer/AGENTS.md, /workspace/.agents/skills/code-security/AGENTS.md -- an exact match, in identity and count, to probe1's hardcoded 'full-file' candidate list. This is direct first-hand confirmation (not merely re-deriving from the same files the probe reads) that the enumerated always-on injection set is neither missing an item nor padded with an extra one, for this checkout/session type. CONCLUSION: could not falsify any headline number (full_model=54643, occupancy_c4=57782, dominant=.agents/skills/code-security/AGENTS.md@27525 tok, gap_c4_vs_occ=0.0006, bad_omit_gap=0.4861) using either a from-scratch reimplementation, a second independent tokenizer library, raw coreutils byte counts, or direct inspection of my own injected context. Found and recorded one real (but non-blocking-for-this-headline) methodology fragility: probe1's tokenizer fallback is silent rather than fail-fast, so a future tiktoken-less run would silently pack a ~56%-different number under a correctly-relabeled but easy-to-miss tokenizer field; recommend the packer assert tokenizer=='tiktoken-cl100k_base' or hard-fail before writing the receipt. Verified command-center/audit/AUD-0062-always-on-context-budget.json state is still 'BLOCKED' and reviewer.verdict is still 'NOT-REVIEWED' -- I did NOT edit or promote that receipt, per instructions; this review only adds independent-review.json alongside the existing (git-clean) probe outputs.
